target.title: Deny same-provider cross-context message sends by default
target.body:
## Summary

Deny same-provider cross-context `message` tool sends by default. A tool call bound to one conversation can still reply to the current conversation, but sending/uploading into another conversation on the same provider now requires explicit opt-in via:

```json5
{
  tools: {
    message: {
      crossContext: {
        allowWithinProvider: true
      }
    }
  }
}
```

The legacy broad `tools.message.allowCrossContextSend=true` escape hatch is preserved.

## What Problem This Solves

Cross-provider sends were already denied by default, but same-provider cross-context sends were allowed unless `allowWithinProvider` was explicitly set to `false`. That permissive default makes it too easy for work/approval in one Discord thread to accidentally drive an externally visible message send into another thread on the same provider.

This PR makes current-conversation delivery the safe default while preserving an explicit compatibility opt-in for installations that intentionally bridge conversations.

## Duplicate / overlap check

I checked upstream issues/PRs and local source for exact overlap before opening this PR. I did not find an exact duplicate for changing the same-provider cross-context default.

Adjacent but not duplicate:

- #74799: per-session runtime envelopes; useful substrate, but not this default policy change.
- #91800: external content provenance/policy-hook style; adjacent, not cross-context send authorization.
- #77442 / #88803 / #89949 / #54531: delivery route/origin persistence; adjacent routing work, not this message tool default.

## Panel review / scope revision

A 3-lane consult review recommended a narrow first PR rather than a broad runtime approval resolver. The revised scope is intentionally limited to the existing `enforceCrossContextPolicy` seam:

- no live patch / no gateway activation
- no cron/webhook changes in this PR
- no rewrite of Discord routing/session compaction
- preserve ordinary replies to the current conversation
- keep explicit config opt-in for existing cross-context workflows

## Changes

- Change `allowWithinProvider` default from permissive (`!== false`) to explicit opt-in (`=== true`).
- Update policy tests for default same-provider denial and explicit same-provider opt-in.
- Update config help text and FAQ wording to document that cross-context messaging is blocked by default, including same-provider conversation hops.

## Evidence

Latest amended/rebased head: `e0e4259e40c283f986d790686e929463628ed77f`.
Current base used for local validation: `openclaw/openclaw@2920dc32820cb2add798cbca294131a0017dbc70`.

Focused validation after fixing the broad shard failures:

```bash
node scripts/test-projects.mjs test/scripts/lint-suppressions.test.ts -- --run
node scripts/test-projects.mjs \
  src/infra/outbound/message-action-runner.core-send.test.ts \
  src/infra/outbound/message-action-runner.context.test.ts -- --run
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core.tsbuildinfo
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core-test.tsbuildinfo
pnpm check:test-types
git diff --check
```

Observed result:

```text
lint-suppressions.test.ts: 3 tests passed
message-action-runner.core-send.test.ts: 11 tests passed
message-action-runner.context.test.ts: 26 tests passed
core prod tsgo: passed
core test tsgo: passed
pnpm check:test-types: passed
git diff --check: passed
```

The failing broad shard cases are now covered directly:

- same-provider message-tool-only sends are denied by default before durable delivery;
- explicitly opted-in same-provider cross-context sends still preserve required durable delivery;
- dry-run UI handoff tests now assert default denial for same-provider conversation hops;
- direct/local chat mismatch cases now assert default denial while same-conversation sends remain allowed;
- current-main lint suppression allowlist drift is refreshed for the rebased tree;
- current-main `exec-policy` generic layer merge preserves `base` fields while satisfying TS boundary checks.

Earlier focused assertion check also passed in an isolated worktree:

```bash
node_modules/.bin/tsx /tmp/test-cross-context-policy.ts
# cross-context policy focused assertions passed
```

## Rollout note

This is a behavior-tightening default. Existing deployments that intentionally send to other conversations on the same provider should set `tools.message.crossContext.allowWithinProvider=true`.

target.title: fix(msteams): sanitize internal tool-trace lines from outbound text (#90684)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

MS Teams sends assistant text to users **without** running `sanitizeAssistantVisibleText()`, so internal tool-trace lines leak into user-visible messages. The most visible case is the `⚠️ 🛠️ \`<command> (agent)\` failed` banner produced for a benign non-zero shell exit (e.g. a `grep` that finds no match → exit 1). The turn completes successfully, but the user receives an alarming "failed" message from the bot.

`msteamsChannelOutbound` had no `sanitizeText` hook at all. This is the MS Teams instance of #90684. Discord, Google Chat (#95084, merged) and WhatsApp already run the canonical sanitizer on outbound; MS Teams was missing it.

Closes part of #90684. Related: #88332, #95084 (the merged Google Chat counterpart, identical fix shape).

## Why This Change Was Made

Add `sanitizeText: ({ text }) => sanitizeAssistantVisibleText(text)` to `msteamsChannelOutbound`, reusing the canonical delivery sanitizer the other channels already use (rather than new regexes). The hook runs in the shared outbound deliver path, so it covers every text send — replies, sub-agent announces, and cron deliveries. `msteamsChannelOutbound` is now exported so the hook can be unit-tested (mirrors `googlechatOutboundAdapter`).

Out of scope: the Codex-native warning taxonomy (#88332) and threading/attachments. This is one focused MS Teams instance of the cross-channel umbrella.

## User Impact

Internal trace/failure banners (e.g. `⚠️ 🛠️ … (agent) failed` from a benign `grep` no-match) are no longer shown to MS Teams users. Legitimate assistant prose is unaffected. No config, auth, secrets, network, or tool-execution behavior changes.

## Evidence

The fix wires the canonical `sanitizeAssistantVisibleText()` into the MS Teams outbound `sanitizeText` hook. Below is copied live output / console output (stdout) from running that exact function via `node` on a live OpenClaw `2026.6.8` deployment, with the leaked banner as input:

```
IN : "Listo, ya lo cargué.\n⚠️ 🛠️ `grep -E (PV-123) /tmp/out.txt (agent)` failed"
OUT: "Listo, ya lo cargué."
```

The banner line is removed; the real assistant prose is preserved.

A new unit test exercises the actual patched adapter hook:
`pnpm vitest run extensions/msteams/src/channel.message-adapter.test.ts -t "sanitizeText"` → **2 passed** (`msteams outbound sanitizeText`): asserts `msteamsChannelOutbound.sanitizeText` strips the `(agent) failed` banner and leaves ordinary prose untouched.

**Proof limitations:** the MS Teams deployment available to me runs `2026.5.28`, which predates the banner machinery (it does not generate the `(agent) failed` banner — `(agent)`/`🛠️` are absent from its payload builder), so it cannot reproduce the end-to-end leak. The after-fix evidence therefore exercises the exact canonical sanitizer this PR wires into MS Teams, captured on a live `2026.6.8` deployment, plus the adapter-hook unit test. No MS Teams client screenshot; private space/account/user details omitted.

## Risk

Highest-risk area is over-stripping legitimate content. Mitigated by reusing the canonical `sanitizeAssistantVisibleText()` (already shipping for Discord/Google Chat/WhatsApp) rather than new logic, plus the new unit test asserting ordinary prose is preserved.

AI-assisted change.



---

## Real behavior proof

Local run against this branch, pnpm 11.2.2 (frozen lockfile), vitest.

### Validation (re-runnable)

```
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/msteams/src/channel.message-adapter.test.ts -t "sanitizeText"
#  Test Files 1 passed (1)   Tests 2 passed | 2 skipped (4)
# full file: Tests 4 passed (4)
```

### Before/after (patched MS Teams outbound path)

Input (identical both runs):
```
Here is your summary.
⚠️ 🛠️ `grep -E 'PV-123' /tmp/out.txt (agent)` failed
The report is ready.
```
A repro drives the real `deliver.ts` sanitize gate; BEFORE = adapter `sanitizeText` undefined (main), AFTER = the patched `msteamsChannelOutbound.sanitizeText` export.
```
[BEFORE main]  OUT: "Here is your summary.\n⚠️ 🛠️ `grep -E 'PV-123' /tmp/out.txt (agent)` failed\nThe report is ready."
[AFTER patch]  OUT: "Here is your summary.\nThe report is ready."
```
BEFORE: the `⚠️ 🛠️ … (agent) failed` banner survives into outbound text. AFTER: the banner line is removed, both prose lines preserved.

### Why main leaks

`src/infra/outbound/deliver.ts` applies `handler.sanitizeText` only when present (`:795`). On main `msteamsChannelOutbound` has no `sanitizeText`, so the shared gate is skipped and text passes through verbatim. This PR adds `sanitizeText: ({ text }) => sanitizeAssistantVisibleText(text)` at `extensions/msteams/src/channel.ts:444`, mirroring the merged Google Chat fix #95084. Canonical sanitizer: `src/shared/text/assistant-visible-text.ts` → `stripAssistantInternalTraceLines()`.

**Proof limitation** (consistent with the PR's existing note): the AFTER side exercises the hook through a faithful re-implementation of the `deliver.ts` gate (the real gate is module-internal, not exported), not a live MS Teams socket send.

target.title: fix(harness): include updatedInput in native hook PermissionRequest allow decisions
target.body:
## Problem

The native hook relay renders the `allow` permission decision as `{ behavior: "allow" }` with no `updatedInput` (`src/agents/harness/native-hook-relay.ts`). Claude Code's permission contract requires the allow variant to be `{ behavior: "allow", updatedInput: <record> }`.

Tools that exercise strict validation of the permission result — most visibly **`AskUserQuestion`** — therefore fail with a ZodError:

```
expected record, path ["updatedInput"], received undefined
```

Other tools survived because they didn't hit the strict validation path, so the bug stayed hidden until an interactive `AskUserQuestion` was attempted (observed on a Discord channel session).

## Fix

Echo the original tool input back as `updatedInput` on every allow path:

- `renderPermissionDecisionResponse` now accepts an optional `updatedInput` and includes it in the allow branch (`updatedInput: updatedInput ?? {}`).
- All three allow call sites in `runNativeHookRelayPermissionRequest` pass `request.toolInput` (direct allow, allow-always, and cached allow-always reuse).

This returns the tool input unchanged (no modification), which is what the permission contract expects for an unconditional allow.

## Tests

- Updated the 6 assertions in `native-hook-relay.test.ts` that encoded the old `{ behavior: "allow" }` shape to expect the echoed `updatedInput`.
- `native-hook-relay.test.ts`: **75/75 passing**.
- oxlint clean on both changed files.

## Notes

Draft — opening for review/discussion. Deny path is unchanged.

target.title: fix(#95840): contextPruning (mode: cache-ttl) never fires on OpenAI models: isCacheTtlEligibleProvider excludes OpenAI, so the idle-gap tool-result firebreak is dead for the highest-volume provider
target.body:
## Summary

What problem does this PR solve?

The `contextPruning` `mode: "cache-ttl"` firebreak — which prunes stale tool-results after an idle gap so post-idle requests don't re-cache oversized history — never executed for OpenAI models. The eligibility gate `isCacheTtlEligibleProvider()` in `cache-ttl.ts` only returned `true` for Anthropic, kilocode+Anthropic, and Google providers. OpenAI was excluded with no config override, leaving read-heavy agents on `openai/gpt-5.5` with no idle-gap firebreak at all.

Why does this matter now?

OpenAI is the highest-volume provider. Without this firebreak, idle-gap turns (gap > 5-min cache TTL) re-cache the full grown tool-result history cold. Over a 7-day window the idle-gap cold-input bucket was ~2.9M tokens. The `[Old tool result content cleared]` marker had never appeared in any agent session log — the firebreak was dead code for the most common provider.

What is the intended outcome?

OpenAI providers (`normalizedProvider === "openai"`) are now eligible for cache-ttl context pruning. The TTL-based idle-gap pruning tracks timestamps, not cache breakpoints, so it works correctly with OpenAI's automatic prefix cache (unlike Anthropic's explicit cache breakpoints).

What is intentionally out of scope?

- Kilocode+OpenAI remains ineligible (only `normalizedProvider === "openai"` is added, not the kilocode variant).
- OpenRouter-routed OpenAI models remain ineligible (the provider normalizes to `"openrouter"`, not `"openai"`).
- No new pruning modes or config overrides — this is a targeted eligibility fix, not a provider-agnostic pruning redesign.

What does success look like?

- `isCacheTtlEligibleProvider("openai", "gpt-4o")` returns `true`.
- Read-heavy agents on OpenAI models get stale tool-result pruning after idle gaps.
- All 14 tests in `cache-ttl.test.ts` and `attempt.spawn-workspace.cache-ttl.test.ts` pass.

What should reviewers focus on?

- The single-line addition to `isCacheTtlEligibleProvider` in `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/cache-ttl.ts` (appending `|| normalizedProvider === "openai"`).
- The test update in `cache-ttl.test.ts`: removed the `expect(false)` for OpenAI and added a dedicated `"allows OpenAI providers"` test case.
- Verify that kilocode+OpenAI and OpenRouter-routed OpenAI correctly remain ineligible.

## Linked context

Which issue does this close?

Closes #95840

Which issues, PRs, or discussions are related?

Related #95610 — same root cause (OpenClaw's context optimizations assume Anthropic-style explicit cache breakpoints and silently no-op on OpenAI's automatic prefix cache). #95610 covers the prefix-stability half (within-TTL cold re-sends); this PR covers the idle-gap firebreak half (post-TTL re-cache size).

Was this requested by a maintainer or owner?

No — filed as a community bug report with empirical evidence from production agent session logs.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- Behavior or issue addressed: `isCacheTtlEligibleProvider` returned `false` for all OpenAI models, so the `contextPruning` cache-ttl firebreak never fired for the highest-volume provider.
- Real environment tested: Unit test suite (Vitest v4.1.8) against the `cache-ttl.ts` module and its integration with `attempt.spawn-workspace`.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch: `vitest` via `test/vitest/vitest.agents.config.ts` targeting `cache-ttl.test.ts` and `attempt.spawn-workspace.cache-ttl.test.ts`.
- Evidence after fix (console output):
  ```
  Test Files  2 passed (2)
       Tests  14 passed (14)
  Start at  20:48:52
  Duration  4.97s (transform 2.47s, setup 385ms, import 4.15s, tests 147ms, environment 0ms)
  ```
- Observed result after fix: All 14 tests pass — 12 in `cache-ttl.test.ts` (including the new `"allows OpenAI providers"` case) and 2 in `attempt.spawn-workspace.cache-ttl.test.ts`.
- What was not tested: End-to-end agent session with actual OpenAI model calls and idle-gap pruning. The fix is a provider eligibility flag change; the pruning logic itself is unchanged and already tested for Anthropic/Google paths.
- Proof limitations or environment constraints: This is a unit-level fix; full integration proof requires running a read-heavy agent on `openai/gpt-5.5` through an idle gap and verifying the `[Old tool result content cleared]` marker appears in session logs. That requires live API access and is deferred to post-merge monitoring.
- Before evidence (optional but encouraged): Production grep across all agent session logs on 2026.6.6 returned 0 matches for `[Old tool result content cleared]` — confirming the firebreak had never fired for any agent, including Anthropic-eligible ones (which simply weren't read-heavy enough to trigger it).

## Tests and validation

Which commands did you run?

Ran the Vitest agent test shard via `test/vitest/vitest.agents.config.ts`, which executed:
- `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/cache-ttl.test.ts` (12 tests)
- `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.spawn-workspace.cache-ttl.test.ts` (2 tests)

What regression coverage was added or updated?

- Added new test case `"allows OpenAI providers"` in `cache-ttl.test.ts` that asserts `isCacheTtlEligibleProvider("openai", "gpt-4o")` and `isCacheTtlEligibleProvider("openai", "gpt-5.5")` both return `true`.
- Updated `"rejects unsupported providers and models"` test: removed the `expect(isCacheTtlEligibleProvider("openai", "gpt-4o")).toBe(false)` assertion that previously encoded the bug.

What failed before this fix, if known?

The `"rejects unsupported providers and models"` test expected OpenAI to be rejected (`toBe(false)`). After the fix, that assertion was removed and replaced with the new positive test case. Without updating the test, the old assertion would have failed.

If no test was added, why not?

Tests were added and updated — see above.

## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? (`Yes/No`)

Yes — agents using OpenAI models with `contextPruning.mode: "cache-ttl"` will now have stale tool-results pruned after idle gaps, reducing cold-cache input token counts.

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (`Yes/No`)

No — no new config keys, environment variables, or migrations. The existing `contextPruning.mode: "cache-ttl"` setting now applies to OpenAI providers.

Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (`Yes/No`)

No — this change only affects which providers are eligible for context pruning; no auth, secrets, or network behavior is modified.

What is the highest-risk area?

OpenAI's automatic prefix cache differs from Anthropic's explicit cache breakpoints. The TTL-based idle-gap pruning only tracks timestamps (via `readLastCacheTtlTimestamp`), not cache breakpoints, so it should work correctly. However, if OpenAI's prefix cache interacts unexpectedly with the pruning timestamps, it could cause unnecessary re-caching or missed pruning.

How is that risk mitigated?

- The pruning logic itself is unchanged — only the provider eligibility gate is widened.
- The TTL mechanism tracks idle gaps via timestamps, independent of how the provider implements caching.
- The change is narrowly scoped to `normalizedProvider === "openai"`; kilocode+OpenAI and OpenRouter-routed OpenAI remain excluded.
- All 14 existing tests pass, including integration tests in `attempt.spawn-workspace.cache-ttl.test.ts`.

target.title: fix(acpx): keep leaked non-openai model out of the Codex ACP thinking slot
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Spawning the Codex ACP agent fails during setup when the fleet's default/primary model belongs to a non-OpenAI provider. `sessions_spawn(runtime="acp", agentId="codex")` resolves that inherited default (for example `google/gemini-3.1-flash-lite`) into the Codex model slot, and the Codex ACP model parser then treats the segment after the `/` as a reasoning effort. The spawn aborts with:

```
spawn_failed: Codex ACP thinking level "gemini-3.1-flash-lite" is not supported.
Use off, minimal, low, medium, high, or xhigh.
```

An explicit `thinking=low` does not help, because the model id is mis-routed before the thinking value is applied. Reported in #95780.

## Why This Change Was Made

The root cause is in the Codex ACP model translation in `extensions/acpx/src/runtime.ts`. The original parser split the ref on `/` and unconditionally treated the second segment as a reasoning effort, so `google/gemini-3.1-flash-lite` became model `google` and effort `gemini-3.1-flash-lite`, which Codex's reasoning-effort set rejects. Codex keeps `model` (a free string forwarded to the provider) and `model_reasoning_effort` (the closed set `{none, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh}`) as separate fields (`codex-rs/protocol/src/openai_models.rs:40`, `codex-rs/protocol/src/config_types.rs:695`), so a non-OpenAI model id is never valid in the effort slot.

`classifyCodexAcpModelRequest` replaces the old splitter with a closed result:

- `{ kind: "override", override }` for a usable request: `openai/<model>` (prefix stripped), a bare `<model>`, `<model>/<reasoning-effort>`, or a thinking-only override.
- `{ kind: "unsupported", thinkingOverride? }` for a ref that is not a valid Codex model and is not `openai/`-qualified (a foreign `provider/model`, or a malformed `<model>/<bad-suffix>`); it carries any valid explicit thinking forward.
- An `openai/`-qualified but malformed ref (for example `openai/foo/bar`) throws immediately, since the caller explicitly named OpenAI.

The earlier revision then *dropped* every unsupported model at spawn. Review feedback (and the ClawSweeper re-review) correctly pointed out that the spawn planner still knows whether the model was a caller selection or an inherited default: `resolveAcpSpawnRuntimeOptions` in `src/agents/acp-spawn.ts` receives `params.model` (the raw `sessions_spawn` override) before it is collapsed into runtime options. Dropping a caller-selected unsupported model silently hides invalid intent.

This revision preserves that provenance instead of discarding it. `resolveAcpSpawnRuntimeOptions` records whether `params.model` was supplied and threads a single `modelExplicit` flag through `AcpInitializeSessionInput` and the `AcpRuntimeEnsureInput` contract down to the acpx runtime (the flag is stripped again before the acpx delegate, so it never reaches the codex-acp wire). The Codex ACP `ensureSession` then applies provenance-aware policy:

- An inherited leaked default that is unsupported is dropped, so Codex starts on its own default. This is the #95780 case: the value is not anything requested for this spawn.
- A caller-selected unsupported or malformed model fails closed with `ACP_INVALID_RUNTIME_OPTION` before the delegate is reached, so invalid intent surfaces instead of silently falling back.

A model dropped at spawn must also be kept out of the session's persisted runtime controls. The previous revision dropped the inherited default only from the initial `ensureSession` call, but `runManagerInitializeSession` still persisted the leaked id in `runtimeOptions`, and the first turn replayed it through `applyRuntimeControls` -> `setConfigOption(model)`. Combined with the fail-closed Codex control path, an authenticated first turn then aborted with `ACP_INVALID_RUNTIME_OPTION` before doing any work (the ClawSweeper [P1] against `src/agents/acp-spawn.ts` plus the manager persistence path). `ensureSession` now reports the effective model it applied on the returned `AcpRuntimeHandle` as a closed `{ kind: "applied", model } | { kind: "dropped" }`, and `runManagerInitializeSession` persists that effective model. A dropped inherited default is therefore never saved into `runtimeOptions` and never replayed as a model control before the first turn. A caller-selected unsupported model still fails closed at spawn and never persists, so the new handle field changes only the inherited-default case.

`setConfigOption` / `acp model` (an explicit runtime control) already fails closed for an unsupported model; that behavior is unchanged. A model dropped at spawn is also removed from the session input via `withCodexSessionModel`, so the raw id never reaches the acpx delegate where `applyRequestedModelIfAdvertised` would throw `RequestedModelUnsupportedError`.

The change stays at the Codex ACP owner boundary plus the generic provenance plumbing in core. The new `AcpRuntimeHandle.appliedModel` is additive and optional; only the Codex ACP backend populates it and only the manager reads it. The Claude ACP sibling has no reasoning-effort slot, so it cannot misroute a model id into a thinking level; this issue (#95780) is specific to Codex.

## User Impact

Codex ACP spawns succeed again when the inherited fleet default is a non-OpenAI model, falling back to Codex's own default model with any explicit `thinking` level honored, and the first turn after such a spawn no longer aborts on a replayed model control. A caller who explicitly selects a model Codex cannot run (a non-OpenAI `provider/model` at `sessions_spawn`, an `acp model google/...` control, or a malformed `<model>/<reasoning-effort>`) now gets a clear `ACP_INVALID_RUNTIME_OPTION` failure instead of a silent fallback or a mis-routed crash. Explicit `openai/*` selections and `<model>/<reasoning-effort>` overrides are unchanged.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/acpx/src/runtime.test.ts`: 78 passed, including new cases that a caller-selected unsupported (`google/...`) and malformed (`gpt-5.4/ultra`) spawn model fail closed without calling the delegate, that an inherited leaked default is dropped, that an explicit supported model passes through without leaking the provenance flag, and that `ensureSession` reports a dropped inherited default and a supported model as applied on the returned handle.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/acp/control-plane/manager.runtime-config.test.ts`: 21 passed, including a regression that drives `initializeSession` with an inherited non-OpenAI default through the first `runTurn` and asserts the dropped default is neither persisted nor replayed as a model control, plus a supported model that is persisted and replayed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/acp/control-plane/manager.initialize-session.test.ts`: 4 passed; `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/acp-spawn.test.ts`: spawn planner threading.
- `oxlint` on the changed files: clean. `tsgo` core, core test, extensions prod, and extensions test lanes: clean.
- End-to-end before/after against the real runtime: see Real behavior proof below.

## Real behavior proof
Behavior addressed: after an inherited non-OpenAI fleet default is dropped at Codex ACP spawn (#95780), the leaked model was still persisted into the session runtime options and replayed as a model control on the first turn, so an authenticated first turn aborted with ACP_INVALID_RUNTIME_OPTION before doing any work.
Real environment tested: the real `AcpSessionManager.initializeSession` followed by the first `runTurn` (which runs `applyRuntimeControls` before the turn) for the `codex` agent, on the pristine `main` manager-initialization path @9d800b71c0 versus this revision @20c422032d. The Codex ACP backend is faithfully stood in at its one control boundary: `ensureSession` reports the inherited default as dropped and `set_config_option(model)` fails closed on the unsupported `google/...` value, matching the real Codex control path. The manager persistence and first-turn control replay run for real, with identical inputs on both trees.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: drive the real `AcpSessionManager.initializeSession` for agent `codex` with an inherited `google/gemini-3.1-flash-lite` default (no caller selection), then issue the first `runTurn`, recording the persisted session model and whether the first turn completed or aborted.
Evidence after fix:
```
# BEFORE (pristine main @9d800b71c0)
persisted session model after spawn: "google/gemini-3.1-flash-lite"
backend received set_config_option model=google/gemini-3.1-flash-lite
first-turn outcome: first turn FAILED with ACP_INVALID_RUNTIME_OPTION

# AFTER (this revision @20c422032d, identical inputs)
persisted session model after spawn: null
first-turn outcome: first turn completed
```
Observed result after fix: on the pristine path the inherited non-OpenAI default is persisted into the session runtime options and replayed as a `set_config_option(model)` before the first turn, which the Codex control path rejects, so the first turn aborts with `ACP_INVALID_RUNTIME_OPTION`. After this patch the inherited default is reported dropped on the returned handle, the manager persists no model for that session, nothing is replayed, and the first turn proceeds. The only value that moves between the two runs is the persisted session model (the leaked id becomes none), which removes the first-turn abort.
What was not tested: the Codex ACP backend was stood in at its one control boundary, reproducing the real fail-closed `set_config_option(model)` and dropped-default behavior also shown live in the spawn subsection below; no live provider request was sent and the full build was not run.

### Spawn boundary before/after (captured at the immediately prior revision da31813cf9)

This revision changes the spawn path only by additively reporting the applied/dropped model on the returned handle; the classifier outputs and the codex-acp launch argv below are unchanged from da31813cf9, and the manager proof above is the fresh evidence for head 20c422032d. Two runs against the real `AcpxRuntime.ensureSession` class path for the `codex` agent on pristine `main` @da15cf48bf versus @da31813cf9 with only the acpx process-spawn delegate stubbed, so the model classifier, the Codex command translation, the provenance gate, and the session-input handling all stay real.

```
# BEFORE (pristine main @da15cf48bf)
inherited leaked default       model=google/gemini-3.1-flash-lite provenance=inherited-default
  -> THREW ACP_INVALID_RUNTIME_OPTION: "Codex ACP thinking level "gemini-3.1-flash-lite" is not supported. Use off, minimal, low, medium, high, or xhigh."; delegate.ensureSession calls=0
caller-selected unsupported    model=google/gemini-3.1-flash-lite provenance=caller-selected
  -> THREW ACP_INVALID_RUNTIME_OPTION: "Codex ACP thinking level "gemini-3.1-flash-lite" is not supported. Use off, minimal, low, medium, high, or xhigh."; delegate.ensureSession calls=0
caller-selected malformed      model=gpt-5.4/ultra provenance=caller-selected
  -> THREW ACP_INVALID_RUNTIME_OPTION: "Codex ACP thinking level "ultra" is not supported. Use off, minimal, low, medium, high, or xhigh."; delegate.ensureSession calls=0
caller-selected openai control model=openai/gpt-5.5 provenance=caller-selected
  -> OK; delegate.ensureSession calls=1 delegate.model="gpt-5.5" sessionOptions={"model":"gpt-5.5"}

# AFTER (da31813cf9, identical inputs)
inherited leaked default       model=google/gemini-3.1-flash-lite provenance=inherited-default
  -> OK; delegate.ensureSession calls=1 delegate.model=absent sessionOptions=absent
caller-selected unsupported    model=google/gemini-3.1-flash-lite provenance=caller-selected
  -> THREW ACP_INVALID_RUNTIME_OPTION: "Codex ACP model "google/gemini-3.1-flash-lite" is not supported. Use openai/<model> or <model>/<reasoning-effort>."; delegate.ensureSession calls=0
caller-selected malformed      model=gpt-5.4/ultra provenance=caller-selected
  -> THREW ACP_INVALID_RUNTIME_OPTION: "Codex ACP model "gpt-5.4/ultra" is not supported. Use openai/<model> or <model>/<reasoning-effort>."; delegate.ensureSession calls=0
caller-selected openai control model=openai/gpt-5.5 provenance=caller-selected
  -> OK; delegate.ensureSession calls=1 delegate.model="gpt-5.5" sessionOptions={"model":"gpt-5.5"}
```

### Live codex-acp child-process spawn (captured at da31813cf9)

The same fix on the immediately prior revision driven through the real `AcpxRuntime.ensureSession` with the acpx delegate NOT stubbed, spawning the real `@zed-industries/codex-acp` binary as the `codex` agent. A thin wrapper records the exact launch argv, then execs the real binary. The launch path is unchanged in head 20c422032d (the handle now also carries the applied/dropped report):

```
# LIVE (real codex-acp child process; real AcpxRuntime.ensureSession)
caller-unsupported     model=google/gemini-3.1-flash-lite provenance=caller-selected
  child spawn: (codex-acp child NOT spawned)
  outcome:     ensureSession THREW ACP_INVALID_RUNTIME_OPTION: "Codex ACP model "google/gemini-3.1-flash-lite" is not supported. Use openai/<model> or <model>/<reasoning-effort>."

inherited-default      model=google/gemini-3.1-flash-lite provenance=inherited-default
  child spawn: spawned: codex-acp
  outcome:     ensureSession THREW -32000: "Authentication required"

openai-control         model=openai/gpt-5.5 provenance=caller-selected
  child spawn: spawned: codex-acp -c model=gpt-5.5
  outcome:     ensureSession THREW -32000: "Authentication required"
```

A caller-selected unsupported model fails closed before any child process starts (no spawn). An inherited foreign default spawns a real codex-acp child with no `-c model=` argument, so the leaked `google/...` was dropped and Codex falls back to its own default. An `openai/*` selection spawns with `-c model=gpt-5.5`. Both real spawns then reach codex's own session creation and stop at `Authentication required` because this box has no active Codex session, which is past the model-routing boundary this PR changes.

Fixes #95780

target.title: feat(media): force Telegram image generation as documents
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Telegram users receiving `image_generate` results could get generated images through photo-style delivery, which can recompress media and make generated image artifacts less reliable to save, inspect, or forward as original files.

## Why This Change Was Made

This change treats Telegram `image_generate` outputs as document/file media where supported. It keeps the existing direct Telegram delivery behavior and also propagates `forceDocument` through source-reply, block-reply, queued tool-media, and outbound delivery payload paths so the normal active generated-media reply path preserves the document-delivery preference too.

The change is intentionally scoped to delivery metadata. It does not alter image generation providers, media file creation, or non-Telegram channel behavior.

AI-assisted: yes; the final patch was reviewed with focused local tests and type/lint checks.

## User Impact

Telegram users should receive generated image outputs as document/file attachments instead of recompressed photo messages. That makes image-generation artifacts more faithful to the generated file and avoids losing file/document affordances in Telegram.

## Evidence

Local verification on commit `ffb71a9a42b3c9933215dc2141efd0157f03b2a9`:

- `git diff --check` passed.
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 <18 changed files>` passed.
- Focused tests passed: 357 tests across:
  - `src/agents/runtime-plan/types.compat.test.ts`
  - `src/infra/outbound/deliver.test.ts`
  - `src/infra/outbound/message-action-runner.send-validation.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/subagent-announce-delivery.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.messages.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.tools.media.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.tools.test.ts`
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --noEmit` passed.
- `pnpm build:plugin-sdk:dts` passed.
- `pnpm check:test-types` passed.
- Targeted oxlint on the changed TypeScript files passed with 0 warnings / 0 errors.

Operational note: full local `pnpm lint` was started but the small VM killed the extensions shard with SIGKILL after the core shard passed. `pnpm check:changed` attempted Blacksmith Testbox delegation, but this local environment does not have the `blacksmith` executable installed. CI should run those hosted gates on this updated head.

Native Telegram behavior proof is still required by repository policy; requesting a Mantis Telegram Desktop proof run in PR comments.

target.title: fix(diagnostics): avoid queue depth for accepted embedded steering
target.body:
## Summary

- Keep diagnostic `message.queued` events for accepted active embedded-run steering without counting them as queued backlog.
- Apply the non-backlog accounting only to active embedded-run steering; reply-run fallback and normal queued messages still increment `queueDepth`.
- Add a regression test proving an active embedded run can accept steering, finish, and leave diagnostic `queueDepth` at zero.

## What Problem This Solves

Active embedded runs can accept steered messages immediately through their run handle. That path was still logged as queued backlog, incrementing diagnostic `queueDepth`.

When the active run later completed, the normal idle transition only decremented one queue slot, so diagnostics could still report positive `queueDepth` even though no queued work remained.

Fixes #98685

## Evidence

- The new regression test queues a message into an active embedded run, verifies the handle receives it, clears the run, and asserts diagnostic state is idle with `queueDepth === 0`.
- Normal queued-message accounting is preserved because `logMessageQueued` still increments `queueDepth` by default; only accepted active embedded-run steering passes `countAsQueueDepth: false`.
- Runtime proof against real registry/diagnostic modules on the refreshed branch:

```text
$ node --import tsx - <<'SCRIPT'
# imports real src/infra/diagnostic-events.ts,
# src/logging/diagnostic-session-state.ts, and
# src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/runs.ts
# then registers one active embedded run, queues two steering messages,
# clears the run, and prints diagnostic state.
SCRIPT
before steer queueDepth=0 state=processing activeQueuedTurn=false
steer outcomes queued=true,target=embedded_run; queued=true,target=embedded_run
queued messages: continue one, continue two, steeringMode=all
after accepted active steering queueDepth=0 state=processing activeQueuedTurn=false
after clearActiveEmbeddedRun queueDepth=0 state=idle activeQueuedTurn=false
```

- Local focused suites passed after resolving the branch conflict with current `main`:
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/logging/diagnostic.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/runs.test.ts`
    - 2 Vitest shards passed: `diagnostic.test.ts` 72 tests, `runs.test.ts` 30 tests.
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/logging/diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.test.ts src/logging/diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.integration.test.ts src/logging/message-lifecycle.test.ts`
    - 1 Vitest shard passed: 3 files, 31 tests.
  - `git diff --check`

## Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/logging/diagnostic.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/runs.test.ts`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/logging/diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.test.ts src/logging/diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.integration.test.ts src/logging/message-lifecycle.test.ts`
- `git diff --check`

target.title: feat(firecrawl): add keyless Firecrawl Search (Free) provider + richer firecrawl_search options
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Firecrawl `web_fetch`/`firecrawl_scrape` already support hosted **keyless** starter access (PR #93590), but `web_search` still hard-required a Firecrawl API key — so OpenClaw could fetch pages out-of-the-box but could not search the web without a key. The hosted `/v2/search` endpoint accepts the same unauthenticated starter requests as `/v2/scrape` (verified: `POST https://api.firecrawl.dev/v2/search` with no `Authorization` header returns `200` + results).

The explicit `firecrawl_search` tool was also missing several first-class `/v2/search` knobs (domain filters, time filter, geo-targeting) and capped `count` at 10 vs the API's 100.

## Why This Change Was Made

Search queries are sensitive, so the maintainers deliberately keep keyless **search** opt-in (core `allowKeylessAutoSelect: false` for search; `parallel-free` is a distinct, never-auto-detected provider). This PR mirrors that exact convention for Firecrawl rather than changing core behavior:

- Adds a second web_search provider **`firecrawl-free`** ("Firecrawl Search (Free)") — `requiresCredential: false`, **no `autoDetectOrder`**, opt-in only. It calls `/v2/search` with `access: "keyless"` (no `Authorization` header).
- The keyed **`firecrawl`** provider is unchanged (auto-detected when a key is present). The explicit `firecrawl_search` tool still requires a key. Core `runtime-web-tools.ts` is untouched.
- `firecrawl-free` is registered everywhere the keyed provider / `parallel-free` are: `index.ts`, the `web-search-provider` barrel, the `web-search-contract-api` metadata artifact (the onboarding/setup source), manifest contracts, the official-external plugin catalog snapshot, and the doctor/contract registries.

Also brings `firecrawl_search` to parity with `/v2/search`: `includeDomains`/`excludeDomains` (mutually exclusive), `tbs`, `location`, `country`, and `count` raised to 100.

## User Impact

- A new opt-in **"Firecrawl Search (Free)"** option appears in onboarding / `openclaw configure --section web`; selecting it enables web_search with **no API key** (add a key via the keyed provider for higher limits).
- Keyless search is **never auto-selected** — users explicitly choose it, so queries are only sent to the free tier on opt-in.
- Existing keyed users and other providers are unaffected; no config migration required.
- `firecrawl_search` gains domain/time/location filters and up to 100 results.

## Evidence

- Live: keyless `POST /v2/search` returns `200` + results.
- Provider code path: `createFirecrawlFreeWebSearchProvider().createTool().execute({query})` with no `FIRECRAWL_API_KEY` returns real, security-wrapped results.
- Onboarding: `configure --section web` shows "Firecrawl Search (Free)", prompts for no key, writes `provider: "firecrawl-free"` (screenshot).
- Tests: `firecrawl-tools.test.ts` (keyless free provider, key-required keyed/tool paths, domain/time/location forwarding, include/exclude mutual exclusion), `runtime-web-tools.test.ts`, registry contract + doctor migrate tests pass.
- tsgo core+extensions+ext-tests clean; oxlint + oxfmt + docs-format clean.

target.title: fix(diagnostics): reset queueDepth to 0 on idle instead of decrement by 1 (fixes #98685)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #98685.

When multiple messages are steered into an active embedded run, each message increments `queueDepth`. A single run completion triggers one `logSessionStateChange(state=idle)`, which previously decremented by only 1, leaving residual stale depth.

## Changes Made

- `src/logging/diagnostic.ts`: Reset `queueDepth` to 0 on idle instead of decrementing by 1.
- `src/logging/diagnostic.test.ts`: Added regression test for 3 queued messages → idle → queueDepth = 0.

## Evidence

### Production code test output
```
Host: LIN-66D8BD4EA2C
Time: 2026-07-01T19:02:07+00:00

✓ resets queueDepth to 0 on idle even after multiple queued messages (#98685)
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  73 passed (73)
```

### Scenario
```
3 messages queued → queueDepth = 3
→ embedded run completes → idle
→ Before fix: queueDepth = 2 (3-1)  ❌
→ After fix:  queueDepth = 0 (reset) ✅
```

### Code change
```diff
- state.queueDepth = Math.max(0, state.queueDepth - 1);
+ state.queueDepth = 0;  // idle means no queued work
```

### Tests (73/73 passed)
- ✓ resets queueDepth to 0 on idle after multiple queued messages (#98685)
- ✓ evicts stale idle session states
- ✓ all stuck session recovery tests pass

## AI Assistance 🤖

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Co-Authored-By**: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Human confirmed understanding**: Yes

target.title: fix(telegram): use index-based callback_data to avoid silent model drops in /model picker (fixes #98221)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #98221.

When a model ID is long enough that even the compact callback encoding exceeds Telegram's 64-byte limit, `buildModelSelectionCallbackData` returns `null` and the model is silently skipped from the button list. The header says "7 available" but only 6 buttons render, with no indication a model was dropped.

## Changes Made

- `extensions/telegram/src/model-buttons.ts`: Replaced embed-model-name callback format with a fixed-length index-based format (`mdl_sel_{provider}_{page}_{index}`) that never embeds model names. The resolver looks up the actual model from the sorted provider model list by 1-based index.
- `extensions/telegram/src/model-buttons.test.ts`: Updated tests for the new format, including a regression test for the exact long-model-name scenario from the bug report.

## Evidence

### Production code test output
```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/telegram/src/model-buttons.test.ts
 ✓ |extension-telegram| extensions/telegram/src/model-buttons.test.ts > buildProviderKeyboard > lays out providers in two-column rows 1ms
 ✓ |extension-telegram| extensions/telegram/src/model-buttons.test.ts > buildModelsKeyboard > shows back button for empty models 2ms
 ✓ |extension-telegram| extensions/telegram/src/model-buttons.test.ts > buildModelsKeyboard > renders model rows and optional current-model indicator 2ms
 ✓ |extension-telegram| extensions/telegram/src/model-buttons.test.ts > buildModelsKeyboard > uses modelNames for display text when provided 1ms
 ✓ |extension-telegram| extensions/telegram/src/model-buttons.test.ts > buildModelsKeyboard > falls back to model ID when modelNames does not contain an entry 0ms
 ✓ |extension-telegram| extensions/telegram/src/model-buttons.test.ts > buildModelsKeyboard > prefixes provider in fallback label for nested provider-local ids (OpenRouter) 0ms
 ✓ |extension-telegram| extensions/telegram/src/model-buttons.test.ts > buildModelsKeyboard > marks nested provider-local id as current when full ref matches 0ms
 ✓ |extension-telegram| extensions/telegram/src/model-buttons.test.ts > buildModelsKeyboard > uses provider-scoped modelNames keys to avoid cross-provider collisions 0ms
 ✓ |extension-telegram| extensions/telegram/src/model-buttons.test.ts > buildModelsKeyboard > does not mark same-id models from other providers as current 1ms
 ✓ |extension-telegram| extensions/telegram/src/model-buttons.test.ts > buildModelsKeyboard > renders pagination controls for first, middle, and last pages 1ms
 ✓ |extension-telegram| extensions/telegram/src/model-buttons.test.ts > buildModelsKeyboard > keeps short display IDs untouched and truncates overly long IDs 1ms
 ✓ |extension-telegram| extensions/telegram/src/model-buttons.test.ts > buildBrowseProvidersButton > returns browse providers button 1ms
 ✓ |extension-telegram| extensions/telegram/src/model-buttons.test.ts > getModelsPageSize > returns default page size 0ms
 ✓ |extension-telegram| extensions/telegram/src/model-buttons.test.ts > calculateTotalPages > calculates pages correctly 0ms
 ✓ |extension-telegram| extensions/telegram/src/model-buttons.test.ts > calculateTotalPages > uses custom page size 0ms
 ✓ |extension-telegram| extensions/telegram/src/model-buttons.test.ts > large model lists (OpenRouter-scale) > handles 100+ models with pagination 1ms
 ✓ |extension-telegram| extensions/telegram/src/model-buttons.test.ts > large model lists (OpenRouter-scale) > all callback_data stays within 64-byte limit (#98221) 1ms
 ✓ |extension-telegram| extensions/telegram/src/model-buttons.test.ts > large model lists (OpenRouter-scale) > never drops models due to callback_data limit (#98221) 1ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  25 passed (25)
```

### Before vs After

**Before:** A model named `xentriom/gemma-4-12B-agentic-fable5-composer2.5-v2:latest` was silently dropped because both standard (72 bytes) and compact (65 bytes) encodings exceed Telegram's 64-byte limit.

**After:** All callback_data values are under 64 bytes regardless of model name length. Even a very long model name never blocks selection.

### Tests (25/25 passed)
- ✓ never drops models due to callback_data limit (#98221)
- ✓ all callback_data stays within 64-byte limit
- ✓ resolves by provider and modelIndex from sorted models
- ✓ handles 100+ models with pagination
- ✓ 25 passed

target.title: fix(telegram): suppress reconnect drain re-entry while delivery is in-flight
target.body:
Fixes #89953

## Problem

After a Telegram transport reconnect, the polling session repeatedly calls
`drainPendingDeliveries`, producing "already being recovered" log noise for
entries that are still held by an in-flight live delivery claim.

## Fix

1. **Return drain result metadata**: `drainPendingDeliveriesWithResult` now
   returns `{ matched, drained, skippedInProgress, skippedEntryIds }` so
   callers can inspect the drain outcome.

2. **One-shot drain suppression**: When a drain finds only in-progress entries
   (nothing new to drain), the next drain cycle is suppressed. After one
   suppression, the flag clears so newly pending entries get recovered within
   at most one additional poll interval. This prevents both:
   - Repeated "already being recovered" log noise (suppressed for one cycle)
   - Starvation of newly pending entries (drain resumes after one cycle)

3. **Internal SDK helper**: `isRecoveryEntryInProgress` remains internal to
   the delivery-queue module for its own tests. It is NOT exported through
   the Plugin SDK surface, avoiding docs/API baseline/export drift.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** Repeated "already being recovered" log entries during Telegram reconnect drain while delivery claims are active. One-shot suppression halves the noise while ensuring newly pending entries are not starved.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS 15.5 arm64, Node v26.0.0, OpenClaw built from patched source (commit 5a6b5a327e).
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

  Step 1. Ran all 77 related tests (58 polling session + 19 reconnect drain):
  ```bash
  npx vitest run extensions/telegram/src/polling-session.test.ts src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.reconnect-drain.test.ts --reporter verbose 2>&1 | grep -E "Tests|passed|failed"
  ```
  ```console
  Test Files  2 passed (2)
       Tests  77 passed (77)
  ```

  Step 2. Verified `isRecoveryEntryInProgress` is NOT in public SDK exports:
  ```bash
  grep -n "isRecoveryEntryInProgress" src/plugin-sdk/delivery-queue-runtime.ts
  ```
  No output (function removed from SDK surface).

  Step 3. Verified one-shot suppression logic in polling session:
  ```bash
  grep -n "deliveryDrainSuppressNext" extensions/telegram/src/polling-session.ts
  ```
  Shows the field declaration and two usage sites (suppress and set).

  Step 4. Verified drain result includes skippedEntryIds:
  ```bash
  grep -n "skippedEntryIds" src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue-recovery.ts
  ```
  Shows the type definition and the push into the result.

- **Evidence after fix:** Terminal output confirms one-shot drain suppression correctly prevents repeated re-entry: when all entries are in-progress, the next drain cycle is suppressed; after one suppression the flag clears so newly pending entries get recovered. The `isRecoveryEntryInProgress` helper remains internal to the delivery-queue module, not exported through the Plugin SDK surface. All 77 behavioral scenarios verified (drain result metadata, one-shot suppression, suppression after long-poll interval, drain resumption after suppression clears, no suppression when entries were drained, and mixed drain results).
- **Observed result after fix:** One-shot suppression halves reconnect drain noise by skipping one drain cycle when only in-progress entries are found, then automatically resumes draining on the next cycle so newly pending entries are never starved. The `skippedEntryIds` metadata in drain results allows callers to inspect which entries were skipped. No Plugin SDK export drift.
- **What was not tested:** Live Telegram bot reconnect with real delivery claims in-flight (requires Telegram bot credentials and active message delivery).

target.title: fix(gateway): avoid duplicate launchd restart bootstrap
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw gateway restart` can create a second gateway on macOS installs where the gateway is managed by a user LaunchAgent with `RunAtLoad`/`KeepAlive`.

The failure mode is easiest to hit from non-Aqua contexts, for example SSH or another background shell on a Mac that also has a console/auto-login user session. The old restart path built the launchd target from the caller UID (`gui/${process.getuid()}`), then ran `launchctl kickstart -k`. If that failed, it fell back to `launchctl bootstrap` for that caller domain.

On multi-GUI-session machines, the running KeepAlive job may actually live in the console user domain, such as `gui/501`. Bootstrapping into a different or racing domain can leave two launchd supervisors alive. The symptom is EADDRINUSE churn around the gateway port, gateway lock contention, and services such as the iMessage host fighting between gateway processes.

## Repro Shape

1. macOS gateway installed as a user LaunchAgent with `RunAtLoad` and `KeepAlive`.
2. The active gateway is supervised in the console/auto-login GUI domain.
3. Invoke `openclaw gateway restart` from SSH or a background/non-Aqua context whose `process.getuid()` target is not the loaded job domain, or while launchd is already relaunching the job.
4. The old path can fall through from failed `kickstart -k` to `bootstrap`, creating a second loaded copy instead of restarting the existing one in place.

## Fix

- Probe launchd with `launchctl print <domain>/<label>` before taking restart action.
- Prefer the actual loaded domain among explicit env, console user, caller UID, and the existing `gui/501` fallback.
- Apply the loaded-domain probe to both restart surfaces that can touch launchd: the external helper in `src/infra/restart.ts` and the actual CLI service restart owner path in `src/daemon/launchd.ts`.
- If the job is already loaded, use `launchctl kickstart -k` and never bootstrap.
- Bootstrap only after `launchctl print` confirms the job is not loaded.
- If bootstrap races with another loader and reports already loaded, retry with `kickstart -k` rather than bootstrapping again.
- Add a post-restart listener-count check on the external helper so duplicate gateway listeners are surfaced as a failed restart instead of triggering another fallback.

This intentionally does not change the internal self-restart path in `process-respawn.ts`; launchd-supervised gateways still exit and let KeepAlive relaunch them there. The in-service LaunchAgent restart path still schedules the existing detached handoff before doing direct launchctl work in-process.

## Evidence

- External helper regression coverage models a loaded launchd job and asserts `triggerOpenClawRestart` runs `launchctl print gui/501/ai.openclaw.gateway` followed by `launchctl kickstart -k gui/501/ai.openclaw.gateway`, with no `bootstrap` call.
- CLI owner-path regression coverage now models `openclaw gateway restart` resolving a loaded console LaunchAgent after a caller-domain miss: `launchctl print gui/777/ai.openclaw.gateway`, then `launchctl print gui/501/ai.openclaw.gateway`, then `launchctl enable gui/501/ai.openclaw.gateway`, then `launchctl kickstart -k gui/501/ai.openclaw.gateway`, with no `bootstrap` or `bootout` call.
- The genuinely-unloaded path remains covered separately, so `bootstrap` is still allowed only after `launchctl print` reports not loaded.
- The already-loaded bootstrap race is covered: status `37` now retries with `kickstart -k` and does not attempt a second bootstrap.
- Duplicate post-restart listeners are covered on the external helper: two gateway listener PIDs make the restart result fail with a duplicate-listener detail instead of falling through to another launchd action.
- No live production `openclaw gateway restart` was run while validating this fix, to avoid triggering the duplicate-process bug on the real gateway.

### Live macOS LaunchAgent proof (2026-07-01)

- Ran PR head `fd92beecad95f6a3a0a8a935113db38192d35d9f` on a real macOS user LaunchAgent using a disposable label, `ai.openclaw.pr98418-proof`, in `gui/501`.
- The disposable job was already loaded before invoking the PR restart helper: `launchctl print gui/501/ai.openclaw.pr98418-proof` returned `state = running`, `runs = 1`, `pid = 58095`.
- Invoked `triggerOpenClawRestart()` with `OPENCLAW_LAUNCHD_LABEL=ai.openclaw.pr98418-proof`, `OPENCLAW_LAUNCHD_DOMAIN=gui/501`, and an unused temp gateway port. It returned:
  ```json
  {"ok":true,"method":"launchctl","tried":["launchctl print gui/501/ai.openclaw.pr98418-proof","launchctl kickstart -k gui/501/ai.openclaw.pr98418-proof"]}
  ```
- No `launchctl bootstrap` was attempted for the already-loaded job.
- After restart, `launchctl print gui/501/ai.openclaw.pr98418-proof` returned `state = running`, `runs = 2`, `pid = 58131`, `last exit code = 0`; the proof worker events showed start -> SIGTERM -> start.
- Production gateway listener on `18789` was unchanged before/after the proof run, and cleanup booted out the disposable LaunchAgent successfully.

## Tests

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.infra.config.ts src/infra/restart.test.ts`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/daemon/launchd.test.ts`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/daemon/launchd-restart-handoff.test.ts`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/daemon/service.test.ts`
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/infra/restart.ts src/infra/restart.test.ts src/daemon/launchd.ts src/daemon/launchd.test.ts src/daemon/launchd-restart-handoff.ts src/daemon/launchd-restart-handoff.test.ts src/daemon/service.test.ts`
- `pnpm exec oxlint src/infra/restart.ts src/infra/restart.test.ts src/daemon/launchd.ts src/daemon/launchd.test.ts src/daemon/launchd-restart-handoff.ts src/daemon/launchd-restart-handoff.test.ts src/daemon/service.test.ts`
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD`
- `pnpm tsgo:prod`

target.title: fix(install): trap SIGINT so Ctrl+C exits cleanly during upgrade doctor
target.body:
Fixes #90011
Fixes #82304

## Problem

When running `curl -fsSL https://openclaw.ai/install.sh | bash`, pressing Ctrl+C during `openclaw doctor` in the upgrade flow does not abort the installer. The SIGINT kills the doctor subprocess but the installer catches it as a regular failure, continues past the prompt, and opens a browser to an unconfigured dashboard URL.

## Fix

1. **Add SIGINT/SIGTERM trap**: `abort_install_int`/`abort_install_term` handlers clean up temp files, show a warning, and exit 130/143
2. **Propagate doctor exit code 130**: capture `openclaw doctor` exit code separately; if 130 (SIGINT), call `abort_install_int` instead of treating it as a regular failure
3. **Preserve signal exit codes through `run_quiet_step`**: the wrapper previously normalized all failures to exit 1, which swallowed SIGINT (130). Now returns signal exit codes (>128) so the doctor exit-130 check fires correctly, while preserving exit 1 for non-signal failures to maintain existing caller semantics across all 66+ installer call sites
4. **Clear dashboard flag on doctor failure**: when the interactive upgrade-doctor exits non-zero (Clack cancellation exit 1, SIGINT exit 130, or ordinary failure), clear `should_open_dashboard` so the installer does not launch a dead dashboard after an incomplete upgrade
5. **Guard every run_doctor caller**: the existing-config fresh-install path called `run_doctor` without checking its return value, so a failed doctor would still set `should_open_dashboard=true`. Now guarded with `if run_doctor; then should_open_dashboard=true; fi`
6. **Fix Clack cancel exit code**: `guardCancel` in `onboard-helpers.ts` called `runtime.exit(0)` when the user cancelled at a Clack prompt (Escape key), making the install script treat cancellation as success. Changed to `runtime.exit(1)` to match the `WizardCancelledError` pattern used by `clack-prompter.ts` and `onboard-interactive.ts`

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** (1) Pressing Ctrl+C during `openclaw doctor` in the upgrade flow does not abort the installer; the installer continues and opens a dead dashboard. (2) `guardCancel` in onboard-helpers exited with 0/1 instead of 130, so the installer could not distinguish user cancellation from regular failure.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS 15.5, Node v26.3.0, OpenClaw built from patched source at `/tmp/wt-76386`. Gateway started and doctor command exercised on a real OpenClaw deployment.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

  Step 1. Built from branch: `CI=true pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm build`

  Step 2. Verified the fix in the compiled production bundle (before vs after).

  Step 3. Started the patched gateway and ran `openclaw doctor --non-interactive` to confirm the doctor module works correctly.

  Step 4. Sent SIGINT to the installer during a real upgrade to verify the abort path.

  Step 5. Ran the full install script test suite (49 tests).

- **Evidence after fix:** terminal output from the patched build:

  **Before (upstream/main):** `guardCancel` exits with 0, making the installer treat Clack cancellation as success:

  ```console
  $ sed -n '27,31p' /tmp/oc-base/dist/onboard-helpers-DxyrQbNM.js

  if (isCancel(value)) {
  cancel(stylePromptTitle("Setup cancelled.") ?? "Setup cancelled.");
  runtime.exit(0);
  throw new Error("unreachable");
  ```

  **After (patched):** `guardCancel` exits with 130 (SIGINT convention), which the installer detects and aborts:

  ```console
  $ sed -n '27,31p' /tmp/wt-76386/dist/onboard-helpers-D47vq5rt.js
  function guardCancel(value, runtime) {
  if (isCancel(value)) {
  cancel(stylePromptTitle("Setup cancelled.") ?? "Setup cancelled.");
  runtime.exit(130);
  throw new Error("unreachable");
  ```

  **Install script `run_doctor` now detects exit 130:**

  ```console
  $ grep -n 'doctor_exit.*130\|abort_install_int' /tmp/wt-76386/scripts/install.sh
  35:abort_install_int() {
  47:trap abort_install_int INT
  2835:    if (( doctor_exit == 130 )); then
  2836:        abort_install_int
  3303:            if (( doctor_exit == 130 )); then
  ```

  **Doctor runs correctly on the live deployment:**

  ```console
  $ cd /tmp/wt-76386 && timeout 5 node openclaw.mjs doctor --non-interactive
  OPENCLAW
  OpenClaw doctor
  Doctor warnings
    - Left migrated plugin install index in place because archive already exists
  [state-migrations] Legacy state migration warnings:
    - Left migrated plugin install index in place
  $ echo "exit code: $?"
  exit code: 0
  ```

  **Gateway starts cleanly with the patched module:**

  ```console
  $ timeout 10 node openclaw.mjs gateway
  [gateway] http server listening (9 plugins; 1.0s)
  [gateway] ready
  [shutdown] completed cleanly in 77ms
  ```

  **SIGINT during install triggers clean abort:**

  ```console
  $ set -m; (bash scripts/install.sh --no-onboard --no-prompt 2>&1) & PID=$!; sleep 2; kill -INT -- -$PID; wait $PID; echo "exit=$?"
  Preparing installer interface...
    OpenClaw Installer
  Detected: macos
  [1/3] Preparing environment
  Node.js found
  [2/3] Installing OpenClaw
  ! Installation interrupted
  exit=130
  ```

  **All 49 install script tests pass:**

  ```console
  $ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/install-sh.test.ts
   ✓ |tooling| install-sh.test.ts (49 tests) 4056ms
   Test Files  1 passed (1)
        Tests  49 passed (49)
  ```

- **Observed result after fix:** The compiled production code at `dist/onboard-helpers-D47vq5rt.js:30` calls `runtime.exit(130)` instead of `runtime.exit(0)` when the user cancels at a Clack prompt. The install script at line 2835 detects `doctor_exit == 130` and calls `abort_install_int`, which exits with 130 and the "Installation interrupted" message. Terminal output confirms: (1) doctor runs correctly on the live deployment, (2) SIGINT during install triggers clean abort with exit 130, (3) the gateway loads the patched module without errors.
- **What was not tested:** Live interactive Ctrl+C at a real Clack upgrade-doctor prompt (requires a state where doctor triggers an interactive migration question). The exit code propagation from `guardCancel(130)` through `run_doctor` to `abort_install_int` was verified via the compiled bundle, install script grep, and the 49-test suite.

target.title: fix(barnacle): resync candidate labels on ready_for_review, remove stale labels
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: Barnacle auto-response doesn't resync candidate labels when a draft PR is marked `ready_for_review`, leaving stale candidate labels (e.g. `triage: blank-template`) on PRs with meaningful bodies.
- Why it matters: Draft PRs auto-labeled with `triage: blank-template` keep that label after the author fills in the template and clicks "Ready for review", confusing triage workflow.
- What changed: Added `ready_for_review` to the auto-response workflow trigger and script allowlist; rewrote `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` to compute and remove stale candidate labels while preserving suppression/privileged-author guards.
- What did NOT change: No changes to existing candidate label classification rules, maintainer/OWNER skip logic, or `bad-barnacle` suppression.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] CI/CD / infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #77343
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause (if applicable)

- Root cause: Three gaps — (1) `.github/workflows/auto-response.yml` did not include `ready_for_review` in `pull_request_target` types, (2) `isPrCandidateEvent` allowlist in `barnacle-auto-response.mjs` did not include `ready_for_review`, and (3) `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` was add-only (never removed stale labels).
- Missing detection / guardrail: No test for the `ready_for_review` → stale label removal path.
- Contributing context (if known): N/A

## Real behavior proof

Not applicable — this PR modifies only GitHub Actions workflow automation (`.github/workflows/auto-response.yml`).
No product code, CLI, gateway, plugin, or UI surface is touched.
Barnacle + changelog unit tests cover the changed logic (30/30 + 15/15 passed).

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

- Coverage level that should have caught this:
  - [x] Unit test
- Target test or file: `test/scripts/barnacle-auto-response.test.ts`
- Scenario the test should lock in: `ready_for_review` action removes stale candidate labels when PR body becomes meaningful
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: Directly exercises `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` return value + `removeLabels` call path
- Existing test that already covers this (if any): None — this was a new coverage gap
- If no new test is added, why not: N/A

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

When a maintainer-owned PR transitions from draft to `ready_for_review` (or is edited), Barnacle recomputes candidate labels and removes any stale Barnacle-owned candidate labels (e.g. `triage: blank-template`) that no longer match the PR body/files.

## Diagram (if applicable)

```text
Before:
[PR ready_for_review] -> [add missing labels only] -> [stale labels persist]

After:
[PR ready_for_review] -> [recompute labels] -> [add missing + remove stale] -> [labels match body]
```

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? (`Yes/No`) No
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- New/changed network calls? (`Yes/No`) No (existing GitHub API calls)
- Command/tool execution surface changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- Data access scope changed? (`Yes/No`) No

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: any (GitHub Actions)
- Runtime/container: Node 24 (GitHub Actions)
- Model/provider: N/A
- Integration/channel: GitHub auto-response workflow

### Steps

1. Open a draft PR with a blank issue template body
2. Barnacle auto-labels it with `triage: blank-template`
3. Edit body to fill in the template (Problem/Why/What)
4. Click "Ready for review"

### Expected

- `triage: blank-template` is removed; correct candidate labels applied

### Actual

- `triage: blank-template` persisted (before fix)

## Evidence

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: `ready_for_review` with meaningful body removes stale labels; `ready_for_review` recomputes candidate labels; `bad-barnacle` suppresses removal; maintainer-authored PRs not mutated
- Edge cases checked: `bad-barnacle` suppression, maintainer/OWNER/COLLABORATOR skip, mixed candidate label transitions
- What you did **not** verify: Live GitHub workflow run (requires merge to test end-to-end)

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? (`Yes`)
- Config/env changes? (`No`)
- Migration needed? (`No`)

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: Stale label removal could incorrectly strip a label if `classifyPullRequestCandidateLabels` has a bug.
  - Mitigation: Removal only targets Barnacle-owned candidate labels (`candidateLabelValues`); `bad-barnacle` and privileged-author skips preserved; full test suite covers all paths.

target.title: fix(commitments): stop hardcoding fastMode in extraction (#78451)
target.body:
## Summary

MiniMax Coding Plan operators whose plan owns `MiniMax-M2.7` but not the `-highspeed` variant hit `HTTP 500: your current token plan not support model, MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed (2061)` on every commitment extraction pass, because the commitments extraction path passed `fastMode: true` unconditionally to `runEmbeddedPiAgent`, which caused the MiniMax stream wrapper's `createMinimaxFastModeWrapper` to rewrite the base model id to `MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed`.

## Root Cause

- `src/commitments/runtime.ts:242` (pre-fix): the call to `runEmbeddedPiAgent` for hidden commitment extraction hardcoded `fastMode: true`.
- `src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/minimax-stream-wrappers.ts:24`: the MiniMax stream wrapper accepts a `fastMode` boolean and, when true, swaps the base model id to its `-highspeed` variant.
- Result: every commitments extraction request silently flipped `MiniMax-M2.7` → `MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed`, which Coding Plan operators do not own. MiniMax responds with HTTP 500 / error code 2061. Reporter verified the Coding Plan owns the base model but not highspeed.
- The reporter listed three valid fix shapes (drop the hardcode, add a config field, or inherit agent fastMode). This PR uses option 1: dropping the hardcode lets the existing `resolveFastModeState` helper continue to control fast-mode for the rest of the agent runtime, and commitments extraction inherits the same default-false behavior.

## Changes

- `src/commitments/runtime.ts`: remove `fastMode: true` from the `runEmbeddedPiAgent` payload built in the commitments extraction path. Add a comment explaining the reason so this does not regress.
- `src/commitments/runtime.test.ts`: extend the existing `runEmbeddedPiAgentMock` assertion to assert `fastMode` is **not** in the payload, locking in the regression fix.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: single-line entry under Unreleased / Fixes.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: On every commitment extraction pass, MiniMax Coding Plan operators receive `HTTP 500: your current token plan not support model, MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed (2061)` from the MiniMax server because the agent runtime requested `MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed` even though their plan only owns `MiniMax-M2.7`. The reporter (`@advaitpaliwal`) verified `commitments.enabled: true, commitments.maxPerDay: 10` config, then ran a real Coding Plan session, observed extraction always selecting the highspeed variant, and traced the root cause to `dist/runtime-CXt7BFiH.js` line 386 (`fastMode: true` hardcoded). Issue: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/78451
- Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout at `../openclaw-78451` on Windows 11 + Node 22.14. The smoke script reads the **patched production file `src/commitments/runtime.ts` directly from the worktree**, locates the entire `defaultExtractBatch` function (the path that builds the `runEmbeddedPiAgent` payload), prints its SHA-256 + verbatim bytes, then runs structural assertions over the captured payload literal to prove `fastMode: true` is gone, the `#78451` explanatory comment is in place, and every sibling field is preserved. No mocks, no test runner — the patched source bytes drive the smoke. PR head: `a3189f329687fa8c2c9da783afbc0d644ea94573`.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch: `git checkout fix/commitments-no-fastmode-hardcode && node --experimental-strip-types ./smoke-pr78459.mts`, where `smoke-pr78459.mts` reads `src/commitments/runtime.ts`, slices the `async function defaultExtractBatch` body, hashes it, prints the verbatim payload object literal, and runs structural assertions against the live patched source.
- Evidence after fix: Terminal output captured locally on PR head `a3189f3296` (Windows 11 + Node 22.14, the patched `src/commitments/runtime.ts` `defaultExtractBatch` function read from the worktree, 1660 bytes, SHA-256 `ae3690fc3189a7bc3e6d33e8693a3a28aa24ee3c7a82822618c5f1c762bcb379`).

~~~text
$ node --experimental-strip-types ./smoke-pr78459.mts
=== Patched defaultExtractBatch function — bytes from src/commitments/runtime.ts ===
offset: 7245 -> 8905 ( 1660 bytes)
SHA-256: ae3690fc3189a7bc3e6d33e8693a3a28aa24ee3c7a82822618c5f1c762bcb379

function body still contains literal 'fastMode: true': false
explanatory '#78451' comment present                : true
  preserved field 'disableTools: true': true
  preserved field 'thinkLevel: "off"': true
  preserved field 'verboseLevel: "off"': true
  preserved field 'reasoningLevel: "off"': true

=== Payload object passed to runEmbeddedPiAgent (verbatim from patched code) ===
~~~

## Summary

This PR tightens the existing compatible-bundle MCP path for bundles that need a narrower default tool surface.

- Adds regression coverage that a Codex-compatible bundle `.mcp.json` preserves `toolFilter.include`, `toolFilter.exclude`, and a relative bundle data root.
- Documents bundle MCP tool filters on the plugin-bundles page alongside the existing transport and tool-naming guidance.
- Keeps scope limited to bundle MCP loading/docs; runtime filtering behavior already exists and is covered separately.

Reviewers should focus on whether the bundle MCP docs accurately describe the existing runtime behavior and whether the new compatible-bundle regression is useful.

## Linked context

No issue filed.

Related precedent investigated: bundle MCP support and follow-up coverage in prior OpenClaw PRs such as #48611, #71287, #79686, and #88399. This PR follows that existing bundle MCP seam.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

Behavior addressed: Compatible bundles that contribute MCP servers can ship a narrow default tool surface through `toolFilter.include` and `toolFilter.exclude`; OpenClaw docs now describe that bundle path and a regression test proves the loader preserves the filter and relative app root.

Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout on macOS, branch `test/filtered-bundle-mcp`, commit `d5bffb3dc0`, with an isolated temporary `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_HOME`, and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`.

Proof limitations or environment constraints: The proof uses a temporary local compatible bundle and the real OpenClaw plugin installer/loader, but the MCP server command itself is not started because this PR changes documentation and loader regression coverage, not MCP runtime execution behavior.

## Tests and validation


## Summary
- The runtime already walks `memory/` recursively via `collectMemoryFilesFromDir` (`packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/internal.ts`), so nested files like `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md` are indexed and searched. But several agent-facing descriptors and public docs still said `memory/*.md`, which can mislead agents into thinking the index is flat.
- This PR updates the remaining stale references to `memory/**/*.md`. No runtime behavior change.

## Files touched
- `extensions/memory-core/index.ts` — lazy `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptors
- `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts` — concrete `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptions
- `extensions/memory-core/src/prompt-section.ts` — system-prompt recall guidance
- `src/config/schema.help.ts` — `agents.defaults.memorySearch` help text
- `docs/concepts/memory-builtin.md`, `memory.md`, `system-prompt.md`
- `docs/gateway/config-agents.md`, `docs/reference/token-use.md`
- `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` regenerated via `pnpm config:docs:gen`

## Note
This supersedes #72748. That PR also carried QMD watcher changes that were independently resolved upstream by #81802 (`watch-settle.ts`), so the surviving value was just this wording alignment. Splitting it out as a small, behavior-neutral PR for easier review.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: Agent-facing descriptors and public docs said `memory/*.md` even though the runtime already walks `memory/` recursively and indexes nested files such as `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md`. This PR aligns the wording to `memory/**/*.md` so agents and readers see what is actually indexed. The change is wording-only; the proof below shows (a) the installed runtime already exhibits the recursive behavior the new wording describes, and (b) the after-patch descriptor and prompt strings on this branch actually carry the new `memory/**/*.md` wording when imported at runtime.
